open_points.subject: public_op:model_fields.model_items
open_points.text: A model's declared fields are the fields its model in the specification lists
open_points.question: When the supplied value is an instance of pydantic's BaseModel but its class is not one of the models listed in the specification, is it a model for this operation, and if so which fields must be returned?
options: Every BaseModel instance is a model; return the fields declared by its runtime model class in that class's declared order.
Only instances of specification-declared model classes are models; answer that every other BaseModel instance is no model.
Every BaseModel instance is initially a model, but one whose declaration cannot satisfy the specification-model restrictions is answered as no model.
open_points.default_guess: Treat every BaseModel instance as a model and return the fields declared by its runtime model class, because the received State 3 obligation says a model is any instance of BaseModel and model_fields knows no specification model types.

witness.initial: A caller holds an instance of a third-party BaseModel subclass ExternalValue with one declared field x; the class is not listed in models.
events: module:operations supplies that value to model_fields.model_items.
model_fields classifies it using the BaseModel boundary stated in State 3.
outcomes: The operation answers [("x", value.x)] because every BaseModel instance is a model and its runtime class declares x.
The operation answers that the value is no model because ExternalValue has no model entry in the specification.
witness.observer: module:operations, and ultimately any caller whose traversal encounters that value

open_points.subject: public_op:model_fields.model_items reflection procedure
open_points.text: Its values are those the model holds for those fields.
open_points.question: Which hidden reflection procedure reads exactly the accepted declared fields, in their declared order, without admitting aliases, computed fields, private attributes, extras or inherited fields?
options: Use pydantic's public class field metadata in mapping order and read each corresponding instance value.
Have the models emitter attach an ordered declaration descriptor that model_items reads without naming individual model classes.
Use model iteration only after factory_checks prove for every emitted model that it yields exactly the required name/value sequence.
open_points.default_guess: Use pydantic's public class field metadata in mapping order and read the corresponding instance attributes.
consequences: Using pydantic's public metadata is compact and generic but couples generation to the selected pydantic API and version.
An emitter-provided descriptor isolates model_items from pydantic reflection details but adds generated metadata that factory_checks must keep aligned with model declarations.
Proved model iteration uses a small runtime path but requires factory_checks to reject any emitted model or dependency version whose iteration includes, excludes or reorders a field.
open_points.requirement: For a model, its declared fields as name and value pairs in their declared order, a nested model given as a value and not opened; for any other value, that it is no model.

open_points.subject: module:model_fields and module:models third-party imports
open_points.text: No other generated module imports it; `models`, which the Factory's models emitter writes, defines its classes on that base class by itself.
open_points.rule: `stdlib_by_module` и `third_party_by_module` — module → список полных import строк, необходимых конкретному модулю. Для записи в этих таблицах projector обязан перенести import в local spec без поиска имени библиотеки в notes или contracts. Глобальные `stdlib`/`third_party` остаются каталогом допустимых imports; module-scoped таблицы являются структурным доказательством необходимости. Не объявленный там module import может быть сужен только по связанному импортом symbol/type, но не по совпадению сырого текста import statement с prose
open_points.question: The passage must declare `from pydantic import BaseModel` in `imports.third_party_by_module["models"]` as well as for `model_fields`, or cease saying that the generated `models` module directly defines its classes on that base class.
